title: Correcting a charting error
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.
The exercise has not been tested with learners, and its Arabic version has not been written.
Electronic correction methods differ by system; only the principle is stated.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
objectives: Correct a paper charting error without hiding it.

sources.use: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals 2.5: documentation principles and error correction

required_sources: The employer's policy on corrections, including electronic records
setup: A fictional nurse notices a mistaken entry on a paper chart.
stem: What is the correct way to deal with the mistaken entry?

options.text: Draw a single line through it, write 'mistaken entry' above with your initials, and then write the correct entry.
options.feedback: Errors are corrected with a single line, the words 'mistaken entry' and initials; they are not erased.

options.text: Cover it with correction fluid and write over it.
options.feedback: Errors should never be erased, scribbled out or covered with white-out.

options.text: Scribble it out so it cannot be read.
options.feedback: The original entry must remain readable so the record can be reviewed.

options.text: Leave it and hope no one notices.
options.feedback: A known error is corrected so later readers are not misled.
